title: NAT and port forwarding
summary: Build what every home router does: share one public address with a private network, then expose one inside service to the internet.

nodes.router: your home router: 10.18.1.254 inside, 203.0.113.1 on the internet
nodes.nas: a home file server with a web page on port 8080, 10.18.1.20
nodes.website: a public website on the internet, 203.0.113.80

tasks.title: Get the laptop online
tasks.text: From **laptop**, `curl http://203.0.113.80/` hangs. The request reaches the website, but the website has no route back to a private `10.18.1.x` address. On the **router**, add source NAT (masquerading) so home traffic leaves with the router's public address.
hints: Prove where it breaks first: run `tcpdump -ni any port 80` on the router while the laptop curls. Requests go out with source 10.18.1.10 and nothing comes back.
NAT rules live in the `nat` table, and source NAT happens in the `POSTROUTING` chain, after the routing decision.

tasks.title: What the internet sees
tasks.text: The website prints the address it saw the request come from. Which address does it report for the laptop now?
hints: Just read the page: `curl http://203.0.113.80/` from the laptop.

solution.note: The website sees the router's public address. It has no idea the laptop exists. The router remembers the translation in its connection-tracking table and rewrites the replies back to 10.18.1.10.

tasks.title: Forward a port to the NAS
tasks.text: You want to reach the NAS web page from outside. Make `http://203.0.113.1:8080/` (the router's public address) reach the **nas** at `10.18.1.20:8080`. Test it from **website**, which stands in for anyone on the internet.

checks.fail_msg: From the internet, http://203.0.113.1:8080/ does not reach the NAS yet.

hints: Destination NAT rewrites where a packet is going. It must happen before the routing decision, so it lives in the `PREROUTING` chain of the `nat` table.

tasks.title: Exposed
tasks.text: Load the forwarded page from **website** and submit the share code it shows. Anyone on the internet could now do the same.

solution.note: This is why port forwarding deserves care. One rule put a private file server on the public internet, with no login in front of it.
